title: What I saw and what was there, with lines written
outcomes: Writes two separate notes for a position: what he saw and what was there
Writes a short variation for each, with both sides' moves
Records positions where the two notes agree without inventing a gap

steps.text: This builds on **Annotate your own game before the engine** and on **Five games in a row, one gap sentence per moment**. There you stated how big a gap was. Now you separate its two sides. **What I saw** is only what you looked at in the game. **What was there** is what a measurement finds. Write both for at least three positions per game, each with a short line of moves for both sides.

steps.caption: Black has just played Nxe4. Replay White's reply and the check that follows, then stop. Black's note will say what he saw.

line.say: dxe4: the pawn simply takes the knight.
Bxf2+ is check and takes a pawn.

claims.statement: dxe4 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
The position is at least 300 centipawns in White's favour (depth 16).

steps.text: Compare the two notes. **Saw:** a pawn on h4 that the queen could take. **Was there:** a defender, the bishop on g3. The line is what makes the note usable: *Qxh4 Bxh4*, and the queen is gone for a pawn. A note without a line is an opinion; with a line, someone can replay it and find where it breaks. The line is written from your side of the board first, then the opponent's reply.

steps.prompt: Pick one of the three positions. Write the 'what I saw' column as a player in a hurry would, then the 'what was there' column, each with a line of at least two moves for each side.

steps.text: **When this holds.** You write 'what I saw' before the engine is opened, from memory of the game, including what you did not look at. *Rule of thumb:* if the two columns read the same, you probably copied one into the other. **When it fails:** a line you could not have seen at the board goes in the 'saw' column. **When it does not apply:** quiet positions, where many moves are fine and the columns agree. Write 'agree' and move on.

steps.title: Where the gap lives
steps.prompt: Two of these positions hold a move that was there to be found; one is quiet. Predict which is which, then check.

steps.text: Now without notes. In these positions nothing tells you whether a tactic is hiding. Look first, write the 'saw' column, then decide whether there is anything more. Sometimes the honest answer is that both columns agree.

steps.prompt: Plan the next annotation. Keep it short and written.
